solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: the colon clause (missing skull and tail) practically defines the blank; 'duplicate' and 'living' are throwaway distractors, so only 'intact' (the opposite) offers any pull
S032-01.notes: Missing skull/tail and only rough length estimate -> fragmentary. Intact contradicts; duplicate/living make no sense.

flags: minor: 'outnumbered' and 'bewildered' are weak distractors; only 'alienated' requires reading the outcome clause
S032-02.notes: Divided supporters, then waverers commit and bill passes -> speech galvanized (energized/united) them.

S032-03.notes: Sentence 3 ('Although the wall is extremely long, it is only a few meters wide... similar color') explains the difficulty of seeing it. A misreads the 'although' clause; B (photographs) not in text; D wrong: final sentence extends, not rejects. Claim is factually consistent with astronaut reports.

S032-04.notes: Ocean-type nitrogen in streamside leaves + bears carrying carcasses inland -> salmon bring marine nutrients to forests. A ignores the bear/salmon pathway (trees aren't near ocean water); C about bears' growth unsupported; D reverses causation. Consistent with real marine-derived nitrogen (15N) research (e.g., Helfield & Naiman, Reimchen).

flags: answer cue: D is the only choice that mentions the 'gap' at all, so students can match it to the claim's key word without computing

minor: D's phrasing ('The gap rises from 7 points ... to 21, 26 and 41 points') is noticeably longer and more numerical than the others and is unusual SAT style; consider making at least one distractor also address the gap (e.g., a gap claim that fails at one step)
S032-05.notes: Gaps: 45-38=7, 52-31=21, 48-22=26, 55-14=41, strictly increasing -> D. A only shows virtual falling (in-person not monotone), B and C don't address widening.

S032-06.notes: Text 2: rise used on statements speakers are sure of, functioning as a check inviting listener signal -> rejects doubt interpretation. B contradicts; C overgeneralizes example contexts; D unsupported.

flags: minor: C is the only choice mentioning any time span, so the goal ('how long') makes it a direct lookup
S032-07.notes: Goal is delay length; only C includes 'up to 17 hours'. Consistent with Kabadayi & Osvath (2017, Science).

S032-08.notes: No tailpipe emissions vs. battery manufacturing emissions -> contrast/concession 'Even so'. Therefore, Likewise, In other words don't fit.

flags: minor: the Tollund Man was found by peat cutters, so choice A's 'investigators' is slightly off historically (harmless since A is wrong anyway)
S032-09.notes: Dangling modifier: 'Excavated...' must modify the body. B makes the body the subject and supplies the verb 'was'. A, C, D place investigators/'there'/people after the modifier. Facts (1950, Denmark, peat bog, mistaken for recent murder) are accurate. A is the likeliest trap.

S032-10.notes: Two independent clauses joined by 'however' need a semicolon before and a comma after: 'May; however, repairs...'. A/B are comma splices; C lacks the comma after 'however'. A is the common trap.
